Where did the English establish their first factory in Coastal Andhra?
x:
Machilipatnam (Masulipatnam) was the first trading factory established by the English East India Company in Coastal Andhra in 1611. It was one of the busiest ports on the Coromandel Coast and served as an important centre for the export of textiles, indigo and spices. The English obtained permission from the Qutb Shahi rulers of Golconda to establish this factory. From Machilipatnam, the Company gradually expanded its commercial activities to other parts of South India, eventually laying the foundation for British political dominance. The port remained an important centre of international trade for the English, Dutch and French throughout the seventeenth century.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
n: First English Factory in Andhra – Machilipatnam (1611)
Permission granted by – Qutb Shahi rulers

s: Sri Krishna Devaraya erected a pillar of victory to commemorate his conquest of coastal Andhra at
x:
Sri Krishna Devaraya undertook a series of successful military campaigns against the Gajapatis of Odisha and brought large parts of Coastal Andhra under the Vijayanagara Empire. To commemorate this historic victory, he erected a Jaya Stambha (Pillar of Victory) at Potnuru, near present-day Srikakulam district. This victory symbolised the establishment of Vijayanagara supremacy over Coastal Andhra and significantly weakened Gajapati influence in the region. The conquest of Udayagiri, Kondaveedu, Kondapalli and finally the northern coastal territories formed part of Krishna Devaraya's eastern campaign. However, the commemorative victory pillar was erected specifically at Potnuru.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
